title: Serbian / Montenegrin — Cyrillic to Gaj's Latin alphabet
authority: Serbian standard orthography: Vuk Karadžić's Cyrillic and Gaj's Latin alphabets in one-to-one correspondence; Montenegrin Ś/Ź (С́/З́) by ministerial decision of 9 July 2009
description: The official Serbian (and Montenegrin) Latin script, letter for letter: Ђ→Đ, Ж→Ž, Љ→Lj, Њ→Nj, Ћ→Ć, Ч→Č, Џ→Dž, Ш→Š. Serbian passports and ID cards print names this way in the visual zone, with diacritics (Đ, not Dj).
notes: Lj, Nj and Dž are single letters written with two Latin characters; the engine restores case (Љиља → Ljilja, ЉИЉА → LJILJA). Output uses separate letters, not the digraph code points U+01C4–U+01CC.
Montenegrin С́ and З́ have no precomposed code points: they are С/З followed by U+0301 COMBINING ACUTE ACCENT, matched as two-character sequences (→ Ś/Ź). Their use is optional in Montenegrin.
A stray combining acute (stress mark) elsewhere is kept unchanged; ѐ/ѝ (accent-marked е/и) become è/ì.
Reverse direction is not fully deterministic: dž, lj, nj can also be d+ž, l+j, n+j across a morpheme boundary (nadživjeti).
In 2009 the Ministry of Interior stated that Đ is written as Đ, not Dj, in passports (Danas, 29 May 2009); old SFRY/FRY passports used DJ.
